correctness.rationale: The alternating-gap Cantor coloring gives a proved two-sided h^theta translation law and an upper theta-order boundary-neighborhood law. Parseval converts this into a lower Fourier-energy bound on every sufficiently large multiplicative annulus. Grid-cell approximation transfers the continuous translation lower bound to lattice symmetric differences. Substitution into the exact nonnegative trace-defect identity gives a logarithmic sum on the critical line, a terminal-scale lower bound when gamma>eta, and a fixed-mode lower bound when gamma<eta. Tensor-product factors supply the dimension d scaling, and the source theorem gives matching upper bounds.

originality.rationale: The direct source arXiv:2609.12226 states the fractional critical logarithmic sharpness and the two off-critical power sharpness questions as open in Remark 9.4; it proves only the classical box endpoint and reports numerical evidence for special fractal examples. Searches by source identifier, trace defect, discrete Fourier concentration, Cantor/fractal boundary, translation modulus, Fourier shell energy, and plunge-region sharpness located no theorem giving the all-exponent matching construction. The principal earlier concentration-operator comparison, Marceca--Romero--Speckbacher (2024), uses regular geometric boundaries rather than this fractional self-similar regime. Unindexed concurrent work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem closes all growth-rate sharpness questions in the direct source's Remark 9.4, including every fractional point on the critical line, and supplies a reusable mechanism from two-sided translation moduli to annular Fourier mass and discretized trace lower bounds.
